title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing, burst smoothing, and utilization reporting enhancements
author: Sofia Ramos
merge_outcome: merged after green CI and approvals
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets see unstable latency and oscillating scale when high-priority tenants burst concurrently. This PR implements three coordinated improvements: 1) priority-aware routing in the autoscaler so reserved capacity can be steered to high-priority queues under contention; 2) token-bucket smoothing for burst controls to reduce oscillation during rapid load spikes; 3) enhanced utilization and per-priority reporting surfaced to the Redwood Console and exported as prometheus metrics.

Changes: added a priority routing policy component to the autoscaler that accepts priority weights and soft guarantees; introduced a smoothing parameter on the token-bucket (smoothing_window_ms + alpha) and a guarded decay path to avoid under-provisioning; extended the utilization reporter to emit per-priority utilization, headroom, and burst_consumption metrics and added a lightweight aggregation layer for fleet-level SLAs.

Key files changed: autoscaler/core (routing + policy), autoscaler/tokenbucket (smoothing implementation + tests), metrics/reporter (per-priority metrics and prometheus exporter), console/backend (new endpoints and dashboards wiring), tests/integration (fleet-level scenarios), docs/release-notes.

Migration and compatibility: config schema is backwards-compatible; new priority routing is opt-in via clusterPolicy.priorityRouting.enabled=false by default for safe rollout. Token-bucket smoothing has sensible defaults to replicate previous behavior unless smoothing_window_ms is set. No customer action required unless they want to opt into priority guarantees.

Testing and validation: unit tests for routing logic and smoothing math added; integration tests simulate multi-tenant bursts against a 50-node dedicated fleet in perf-canary; load tests show 25% reduction in scaling oscillation and 12% improvement in p95 latency for high-priority traffic in our synthetic workload. CI: flaky e2e fixed by increasing test timeouts; all checks green at merge.

Rollout plan: staged rollout - canary (10% fleets) for 48 hours, monitor burst_* and utilization_* metrics and error rates, then 50% for 72 hours, then full rollout. Feature gated and reversible via clusterPolicy.priorityRouting.enabled.

Related: ENG-8472 for design doc, PM-412 for product acceptance criteria, SUP-1298 for customer-reported incident motivating the change.

Checklist: [x] design doc signed off, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] console changes behind feature flag, [x] rollout playbook included.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add priority routing policy and config (autoscaler/core), 2) implement token-bucket smoothing and tests (autoscaler/tokenbucket), 3) expand metrics reporter + console endpoints + docs
review_comments: Ethan Nguyen: Nice work — main question is whether priority routing could cause starvation of lower-priority tenants under pathological load. I think we should add a min_headroom_per_priority config and a test for it.
Sofia Ramos: Good point. Added min_headroom_per_priority with a sane default (5% fleet headroom) and added a test case covering starvation scenarios.
Priya Patel: Metrics look good, but can we use histogram buckets for burst_consumption? It'll make alerts easier.
Sofia Ramos: Switched burst_consumption to a histogram with exponential buckets; updated console queries and dashboards.
Liam O'Connor: e2e failed initially due to hard-coded timeouts in the perf harness; please re-run after fix.
Sofia Ramos: Fixed harness timeout issues and re-ran. CI is now green.
release_notes: Enhancement: Priority-aware autoscaler routing, token-bucket smoothing to reduce scaling oscillation, and per-priority utilization metrics exposed in Console and Prometheus. Opt-in via clusterPolicy.priorityRouting.enabled; no action required for default behavior.
notes_to_ops: Rollout is gated. Follow the included playbook: canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Monitor metrics: autoscaler.priority_headroom, autoscaler.burst_consumption_bucket, utilization.per_priority. If error rates increase, flip clusterPolicy.priorityRouting.enabled=false to rollback.
